# Landing Page Design Skill

Use this skill for landing pages, launch pages, SaaS marketing pages, product showcases, waitlist pages, pricing sections, and hero+features compositions.

## Core references

- https://claude.com/plugins/frontend-design
- https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable
- http://uupm.cc/
- https://github.com/facebook/astryx

## Design goals

- Build for a single conversion goal: sign up, book, buy, demo, or request access.
- Keep the message clear and specific: audience, problem, promise, proof, CTA.
- Favor strong hierarchy over decoration.
- Design mobile first, then expand elegantly for desktop.
- Use one dominant accent color and one clear visual rhythm.
- Prefer accessible contrast and clear spacing over decorative complexity.

## Layout system

- Hero: headline, subheadline, CTA, trust indicators, optional product preview.
- Social proof: customer quotes, logos, metrics, feature highlights.
- Benefits: concise benefit blocks with icons and short labels.
- Conversion section: pricing, demos, or CTA with urgency and clarity.
- Footer: trust, navigation, legal links, contact options.

## Typography and rhythm

- Use a clear type scale with strong headings and readable body copy.
- Use generous spacing and consistent alignment.
- Break visual monotony with asymmetry or deliberate composition, but never at the cost of readability.
- Avoid overusing generic UI fonts and low-contrast text.

## Color and visual style

- Choose a palette that matches product context: SaaS, luxury, playful, healthcare, fintech, etc.
- Use an accent color for CTAs and attention points.
- Keep backgrounds clean and avoid chaotic gradients or heavy shadows everywhere.
- Pair colors with accessible contrast and consistent brand logic.

## Motion and interaction

- Add subtle motion only when it supports clarity or feedback.
- Use hover states, scaling, and transitions that are smooth and purposeful.
- Avoid excessive bounce, excessive parallax, or noise-heavy animation.

## Quality checklist

Before shipping a landing page, verify:

- headline communicates value instantly
- CTA is obvious and repeated where needed
- trust signals are visible above the fold
- spacing is consistent and breathable
- layout works on mobile without awkward wrapping
- contrast is accessible
- copy is brief, direct, and benefit-driven
- visual language matches the product and target audience

## Anti-patterns to avoid

- generic purple-blue gradient everywhere
- card-inside-card layouts with no visual hierarchy
- default system fonts and weak type pairing
- hidden or low-contrast CTAs
- too many competing messages in one screen
- noisy animations and decorative clutter
- vague value propositions and generic headings

## Recommended workflow

1. Identify the product, audience, and primary conversion action.
2. Choose a visual direction that fits the brand and category.
3. Create a conversion-first structure: hero, proof, benefits, CTA, pricing or final action.
4. Implement with strong spacing, accessible colors, and polished components.
5. Review the page for clarity, hierarchy, responsiveness, and trust.

## Prompt examples

- Create a SaaS landing page for a B2B AI sales assistant with a premium tech aesthetic.
- Design a healthcare landing page with calm colors, trust signals, and a strong appointment CTA.
- Build a fintech landing page with bold metrics, subtle motion, and a clean conversion funnel.
- Improve this hero section to be more conversion-focused and modern.

Use these references as guidance, but adapt the final result to this project's real product, audience, and brand.
